questions.question_text:
A squash player wins each rally independently with probability $0.6$.
She plays a fixed sequence of $7$ rallies.
Find the probability that she wins exactly $5$ of them, correct to four decimal places.

options.why: Used $r=4$ instead of $r=5$ successes.
Swapped $p$ and $1-p$, using $0.4$ as the probability of winning a rally.
Left out the factor ${}^{7}C_{5}$, so only one arrangement was counted.

questions.question_text:
A high jumper clears a record height on each of her attempts independently with probability $0.15$.
She makes $10$ such attempts over a season.
Find the probability that she clears it exactly twice, correct to four decimal places.

options.why: Used $r=3$ instead of $r=2$ successes.
Used $r=1$ instead of $r=2$ successes.
Found $P(X \le 2)$ rather than the single term $P(X=2)$.

questions.question_text:
A cricketer takes a catch cleanly on each of $50$ chances independently with probability $0.72$.
Let $X$ be the number of clean catches.
Find $\text{Var}(X)$.

options.why: Gave the mean $np$ instead of the variance $np(1-p)$.
Gave the standard deviation $\sqrt{np(1-p)}$ instead of the variance.
Found $n(1-p)$, leaving the factor $p$ out of the variance.

questions.question_text:
A volleyball server lands each serve independently with probability $0.45$.
She serves $20$ times in a match.
Find the standard deviation of the number of serves she lands, correct to two decimal places.

options.why: Gave the variance $np(1-p)$ without taking the square root.
Gave the mean $np$ instead of the standard deviation.
Used $n\sqrt{p(1-p)}$, multiplying the Bernoulli standard deviation by $n$ instead of by $\sqrt{n}$.

questions.question_text:
The number of races a sprinter wins in a season is $X \sim \text{Bin}(n,p)$, with $E(X) = 14$ and $\text{Var}(X) = 8.4$.
Find $n$.

options.why: Took $\frac{\text{Var}(X)}{E(X)}$ to be $p$ rather than $1-p$, giving $p=0.6$ and $n=14/0.6=23.333\ldots$, then incorrectly rounded this inconsistent trial count to $23$.
Divided the variance by $p$ instead of dividing the mean by $p$.
Read the mean $E(X)$ itself as the number of trials.

questions.question_text:
The number of set pieces a footballer scores from is $X \sim \text{Bin}(n,p)$, with $E(X) = 18$ and $\text{Var}(X) = 10.8$.
Find $n$.

options.why: Took $10.8/18=0.6$ to be $p$ rather than $1-p$, then calculated $18/0.6$.
Found $p=0.4$ but divided the variance $10.8$ by $p$ instead of dividing the mean $18$ by $p$.
Read the mean $E(X)$ itself as the number of trials.

questions.question_text:
A water polo team plays $24$ matches and wins each independently with probability $0.25$.
Find the expected number of matches the team wins.

options.why: Used $1-p$, giving the expected number of matches lost.
Found the variance $np(1-p)$ instead of the mean $np$.
Divided $24$ by $0.25$ instead of multiplying.

questions.question_text:
A player takes $6$ shots and scores each independently with probability $0.5$.
Find the probability that she scores exactly $2$ shots, correct to four decimal places.

options.why: Used $r=3$ instead of $r=2$ successes.
Left out the factor ${}^{6}C_{2}=15$, so only one arrangement was counted.
Found $P(X \le 2)$ instead of $P(X=2)$, including the probabilities of zero and one success.
